title: The Manse to Herrengasse 23: the Brothers, the Bern Station, and the Craft of Not Being Photographed
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Manse and the Grandfather's Table

stops.name: Watertown, birth in the manse
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the manse of the First Presbyterian Church, where his father Allen Macy Dulles preaches, Edith Foster Dulles bears a second son and they name him Allen Welsh. The older brother, John Foster, is five years ahead of him and was born in Washington, not here; Watertown is where both boys are raised, in a house of sermons and Sunday discipline, sharing an upstairs hallway. One of them will spend his working life in rooms the public never enters, the other in rooms the public photographs. Their mother's father, John Watson Foster, had been Secretary of State under Benjamin Harrison.
suggested_refs: The manse of the First Presbyterian Church, Watertown, New York, boyhood house of both Dulles brothers
sources: Wikipedia, 'John Foster Dulles' (born Washington, D.C., 25 February 1888, correcting the common claim of a shared birthplace)
Peter Grose, Gentleman Spy: The Life of Allen Dulles (1994)

stops.name: Henderson Harbor, the summers at the grandfather's house
stops.date_confidence: traditional: the summers run through the 1890s and 1900s with no single dated visit
stops.campa: On the Lake Ontario shore the Foster family keeps a summer house, and John Watson Foster, who served Benjamin Harrison as Secretary of State, keeps his grandchildren at the table while the talk runs to legations, treaties, and the handling of foreign ministers. Two of those grandchildren will hold the open and the secret halves of American foreign power at the same time. Their biographer treats these summers as the seedbed of both careers, which is a biographer's causal claim rather than a document. The boys left no diary of it.
suggested_refs: The Foster summer house at Henderson Harbor on Lake Ontario
sources: Stephen Kinzer, The Brothers: John Foster Dulles, Allen Dulles, and Their Secret World War (2013)

stops.name: Princeton, Nassau Hall and the class of 1914
stops.date_confidence: inferred: graduation 1914 is attested, the matriculation year is calculated back from it
stops.campa: He follows Foster to Princeton six years behind him. He graduates with the class of 1914 and takes a master's degree in 1916. One widely repeated chronology puts his degree in 1911, which would make him eighteen at graduation with five idle years before the Foreign Service, and the rest of his own record contradicts it. The society he joins is the American Whig-Cliosophic Society, the oldest debating club in the country, where undergraduates stand up in a hall built for the purpose and argue questions of policy at each other.
suggested_refs: Whig Hall and Clio Hall, Princeton, seat of the American Whig-Cliosophic Society

stops.name: Allahabad, the year of teaching in India
stops.date_confidence: uncertain: the encyclopedias say only that he taught school in India before 1916; the city and school are unconfirmed
stops.campa: Between the degree and the Foreign Service he goes to India and teaches school for a year. The record is thin. The encyclopedias say only that he taught in India; the biographers say Allahabad; nothing reachable settles the town or the institution. What is certain is that a twenty-one-year-old from upstate New York spends the first year of the world war on the far side of the British Empire, teaching boys their lessons, while his brother reads law in New York. He comes back and applies to the Department of State.
suggested_refs: Mission and government schools of Allahabad, United Provinces, 1914-1915
sources: Wikipedia, 'Allen Dulles' ('taught school in India before entering the diplomatic service in 1916')
Peter Grose, Gentleman Spy (1994), for the Allahabad identification, not independently confirmed

stops.name: Washington, sworn into the Foreign Service
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: The Department of State works out of the State, War, and Navy Building beside the White House, a granite pile of columns and chimney stacks that men of the period call the ugliest building in America. Dulles enters the service here at twenty-three, with the war in Europe two years old and America not yet in it. His grandfather John Watson Foster had run this Department under Benjamin Harrison. His uncle Robert Lansing is running it in the year Allen joins, and will hold it until 1920.
suggested_refs: The State, War, and Navy Building, now the Eisenhower Executive Office Building, seat of the Department of State in 1916
sources: Note: sources placing the 1916 Department at 38.8977, -77.0365 give the coordinates of the White House

stops.name: Vienna, the first posting
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: His first station is the capital of Austria-Hungary in the third year of a war it is losing, an empire of eleven nationalities held together by an emperor of eighty-six who will be dead before the year is out. Dulles is a junior man in a legation, watching a state come apart from the inside. He learns the trade of the half-neutral capital: what is said at dinner, and who repeats it afterward and to whom. Relations are severed in 1917 and the legation closes behind him. He is there less than a year.
suggested_refs: The United States Legation at Vienna, closed on the severance of relations in 1917

stops.name: Bern, the call he did not take
stops.date_confidence: attested as the date Dulles himself gave; the call is not corroborated and historians doubt it
stops.campa: Transferred to neutral Bern shortly before America enters the war, the young officer is on duty one evening when the telephone rings and a Russian asks for a meeting at the American legation. Dulles has a tennis date and declines. He will tell this story for the rest of his life: that the Russian was Vladimir Lenin, who left Switzerland the next day on a German train for Petrograd. No corroboration has ever been found, and the story survives in his own telling and nowhere else. Did the telephone ring at all that evening?
suggested_refs: The United States Legation at Bern, 1917-1918
sources: Wikipedia, 'Allen Dulles' (Dulles is the source of the anecdote, not its debunker)
Note: the call is dated to the eve of Lenin's departure from Switzerland, not to the eve of the October Revolution seven months later

stops.name: Paris, the delegation at the Crillon
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the conference; the brothers' arrival dates are not separately fixed
stops.campa: The American delegation to the peace conference takes over the Hotel de Crillon on the Place de la Concorde, and both Dulles brothers are in it: Foster as legal counsel working on reparations, Allen on boundary questions in the successor states. It is their first joint assignment and the shape of the rest is already visible, the elder at the law and the money, the younger at the map and the people who live on it. Their uncle Robert Lansing sits at the table above them both. Foster leaves Paris convinced the reparations settlement is a mistake.
suggested_refs: The Hotel de Crillon, Place de la Concorde, headquarters of the American delegation in 1919

stops.name: Pera, the Protocols exposed as a forgery
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: Posted to the American embassy in the Pera district above the Golden Horn, in a city under Allied occupation with the Ottoman order coming down around it, Dulles takes part in establishing that The Protocols of the Elders of Zion is a forgery, lifted from a French satire on Napoleon III. He is twenty-eight, in his fourth posting in five years. The finding is published. The book goes on selling in a dozen languages, and Henry Ford keeps printing it in Michigan.
suggested_refs: The United States Embassy at Constantinople, Pera, under the Allied occupation 1918-1923

stops.name: Washington, the Near East desk
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the span 1922-1926; the legend often relocates these years to Istanbul, which the record does not support
stops.campa: For four years he runs the Near East division from a desk in Washington. The division covers the wreck of the Ottoman Empire, the mandates, the oil concessions of Mesopotamia, and the American missionary schools scattered from Beirut to Van. He is thirty when he takes it, and the work is cable traffic: what the Department will say, to whom, and in whose name. The legend relocates these years to Istanbul. The record has him at a desk in Washington from 1922 to 1926.
suggested_refs: Records of the Near East division of the Department of State, 1922-1926
sources: Wikipedia, 'Allen Dulles' ('chief of the Near East division of the Department of State', Washington)
Note: geography sources placing this post in Constantinople conflate it with the separate 1921 embassy posting

stops.name: Washington, the law degree and the decision to leave
stops.date_confidence: inferred: biographies give 1926, one chronology gives 1927, the encyclopedias give no year at all
stops.campa: He takes a law degree at George Washington University at night while running the Near East division by day, then resigns from the government. The reason given is money: a Foreign Service officer cannot keep a family in the manner this family expects, and Sullivan and Cromwell can. He has been married to Martha Todd, called Clover, since 1920. Foster is already a senior partner at the firm. He is thirty-three. The biographies date the resignation to 1926, one chronology to 1927, and the encyclopedias give no year at all.
suggested_refs: George Washington University Law School, LLB awarded to Allen W. Dulles

stops.name: 48 Wall Street, joining his brother's firm
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the move is dated to 1926 in the biographies, the month is not given
stops.campa: Sullivan and Cromwell occupies the tower at 48 Wall Street and is the most powerful law firm in America, which in the 1920s means the most powerful law firm anywhere. Foster runs it. Allen arrives as a partner with a decade of legations behind him and a contact book no other man in the building can match. The firm's business is largely the German business: bond issues floated for German municipalities and cartels, and American capital lent into a defeated economy. The paper of the Weimar recovery is underwritten from this address.
suggested_refs: Sullivan and Cromwell's interwar German loan portfolio and its Berlin office

stops.name: 45 East 65th Street, the Council on Foreign Relations
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the directorship; the Council does not move to the Harold Pratt House until April 1945
stops.campa: He becomes a director of the Council on Foreign Relations at thirty-four, later its secretary, later its president. The Council in these years is a townhouse on East Sixty-fifth Street, not the Pratt House it will occupy after 1945, and its membership is the short list of lawyers, bankers, editors, and former officials who work out among themselves what the American interest is. A quarter of a century later he will staff an intelligence service largely out of this membership list.
suggested_refs: The Council on Foreign Relations at 45 East 65th Street, its premises before the 1944 Pratt bequest

stops.name: Berlin, the meeting with Hitler
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the month; the year is attested
stops.campa: Three months after the Nazis take power, Dulles comes to Berlin on the firm's business and is received by Adolf Hitler; he calls on Joseph Goebbels as well. He is there as a lawyer for clients with German exposure, and the question in front of him is whether the new government will honor the old contracts: whether the bonds floated in the 1920s will go on paying. The Reichstag has been burned six weeks. The camp at Dachau opened in March, three weeks before he arrives.
suggested_refs: Sullivan and Cromwell's German client files, 1933
sources: David Talbot, The Devil's Chessboard (2015), cited as the source of a contested thesis rather than as evidence

stops.name: Berlin, the office closed and the date moved
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the visit and the partners' vote are dated to 1935; the month is not fixed
stops.campa: He comes back in 1935 and goes home somewhat disturbed, which is the phrase the record keeps. He then leads the junior partners in forcing a vote to shut Sullivan and Cromwell's Berlin office and its Frankfurt subsidiary. Foster is the only partner who votes against closing. The firm loses that argument and then does something stranger than the argument itself: it backdates the announcement of the closure to 1934, so the record will show it left a year earlier than it did. The extra year is the one nobody wanted written down.
suggested_refs: The backdated 1934 closure announcement of the Sullivan and Cromwell Berlin office

stops.name: Manhattan, the primary he loses
stops.date_confidence: uncertain: the run is attested to 1938; no date, opponent, vote total, or campaign address is reachable
stops.campa: He runs for the Republican nomination in New York's sixteenth congressional district and loses it. Nothing else about the campaign survives in anything reachable: no vote, no opponent, no headquarters. He is forty-five, a partner at the richest firm on Wall Street, and the thing he wants that year is a seat in the House of Representatives. It is the only time in a life spent inside institutions that Allen Dulles asks a public to choose him. What he said to the voters of the sixteenth district is not recoverable.
suggested_refs: Republican primary records, New York's 16th congressional district, 1938

stops.name: Room 3603, Rockefeller Center
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the month
stops.campa: William Donovan recruits him into the Coordinator of Information, the outfit that will become the Office of Strategic Services, and gives him New York: an office on the thirty-sixth floor at 630 Fifth Avenue, along the same corridor as British Security Co-ordination, which is running Britain's covert operations on American soil out of Rockefeller Center while America is still formally neutral. Dulles is the liaison. The war is two months from reaching the country and he is already inside it. The room number is 3603.
suggested_refs: Room 3603, 630 Fifth Avenue, wartime station of both the OSS and British Security Co-ordination

stops.name: Bern, the last man across the border
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He crosses into Switzerland on the twelfth of November 1942, hours before the German occupation of Vichy France closes the frontier behind him. For the rest of the war Bern is a sealed island of neutrality inside the Reich, and Dulles rents an apartment in the arcaded old town at Herrengasse 23, with a terrace and a back garden that let a visitor arrive out of the dark without passing a lighted front door. He does not conceal who he is. Within weeks the word runs through Bern that the American with the pipe is the man to talk to, and people come.
suggested_refs: Herrengasse 23, Bern, the OSS station apartment 1942-1945

stops.name: Bern, the cables of Fritz Kolbe
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the relationship runs through 1943 and 1944; the first delivery is not separately dated here
stops.campa: A German Foreign Office functionary named Fritz Kolbe walks in at Herrengasse offering documents and is nearly turned away as a plant. The British refused him first; Claude Dansey of MI6 goes on calling Dulles a fool who swallows false information easily. Dulles takes him. Over the following months Kolbe hands across cable traffic from the heart of the Reich's diplomatic system, including material on the Messerschmitt Me 262 jet fighter and the identities of German agents then working. The traffic runs through 1943 and into 1944.
stops.quote_source: Claude Dansey of MI6 on Dulles, quoted in Keith Jeffery, MI6: The History of the Secret Intelligence Service 1909-1949 (Bloomsbury, 2010), pp. 380-382, 507, 509-512; the bracketed words are an editorial interpolation
suggested_refs: The Kolbe traffic in the OSS Bern files
sources: Note: 'fool' and 'swallows [false information] easily' are two separate quoted fragments in the source, not one continuous sentence

stops.name: Bern, the priest's network out of Vienna
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the traffic runs through 1943 and 1944; no single delivery date is fixed
stops.campa: Intelligence reaches Herrengasse from an Austrian resistance group gathered around a Catholic priest, Heinrich Maier, working out of Vienna: production figures and locations for the V-1 and V-2 rockets, for tanks, for aircraft. The material feeds Operation Crossbow, the bombing of the rocket sites. The Gestapo breaks the group and Maier is executed. Dulles sits in a warm room in a neutral city, reading production figures that men who are going to be hanged have found the means to send him.
suggested_refs: The Maier-Messner group of the Austrian resistance and its V-weapons reporting

stops.name: Bern, the Schroeder channel and the money leaving Germany
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the contacts are reported for 1944 and 1945; their purpose is contested and no month is fixed
stops.campa: As the war turns, Dulles is in contact with German industrialists and with Kurt Freiherr von Schroeder, the Cologne banker who hosted the 1933 meeting that put Hitler into the chancellery and who now handles SS money. The reported business is the movement of Nazi-linked funds out of Germany. The contacts are reported for 1944 and 1945; the purpose is contested and no month is fixed. What the Americans thought they were buying, and what the Germans thought they were selling, the record does not settle.
suggested_refs: Kurt Freiherr von Schroeder and the Cologne banking channel
sources: Wikipedia, 'Allen Dulles' (reported contacts; characterization of intent contested in the literature)

stops.name: Lucerne, the SS general's offer
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The Swiss intelligence officer Max Waibel arranges a meeting at Lucerne, and Karl Wolff, Highest SS and Police Leader in Italy, presents terms for the surrender of the German forces in the north. Wolff has signed deportation orders. Dulles hears him out. What passes between them, and is not written down for a long while afterward, is an understanding that cooperation now will be remembered when the tribunals sit. Wolff will not stand in the dock at Nuremberg as a defendant. He will appear there as a witness.
suggested_refs: Max Waibel's Swiss intelligence channel and the opening of Operation Sunrise

stops.name: Ascona, the generals on Lake Maggiore
stops.date_confidence: attested for the fifteenth and nineteenth of March; sources placing these meetings near Zurich are in error
stops.campa: On the fifteenth and again on the nineteenth of March, Wolff works out the mechanics of a surrender with the American general Lyman Lemnitzer and the British general Terence Airey at Ascona, on the Swiss shore of Lake Maggiore. Moscow learns of the talks and Stalin accuses the Western allies of arranging a separate peace; Roosevelt denies it in the last weeks of his life. The Joint Chiefs order the channel closed and Dulles does not close it. The two generals come to the lake in civilian clothes, under false names.
suggested_refs: Ascona and the Villa meetings of 15 and 19 March 1945; Max Husmann's Institut Montana on the Zugerberg, the intermediary school

stops.name: Caserta, the surrender signed
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the Royal Palace at Caserta, headquarters of the Allied command in the Mediterranean, the instrument surrendering close to a million German troops in Italy is signed; it takes effect on the second of May. It is the first large German capitulation of the war, and the channel that produced it ran through an apartment in Bern. Historians have argued ever since over what Sunrise bought: days off the end of a war already ending, or a precedent for dealing with men who ought to have been arrested. Gerhard Weinberg holds that Dulles let himself be carried away and acted over the orders of the Joint Chiefs.
stops.quote: Never, not even in the Bay of Pigs, was his capacity for detached misjudgment more disastrous than in his management of Operation Sunrise, as the Wolff negotiations were called.
stops.quote_source: John Kenneth Galbraith, cited in Wikipedia, 'Operation Sunrise (World War II)'
suggested_refs: The instrument of surrender at Caserta, 29 April 1945
Gerhard Weinberg's judgement that Sunrise reflects very badly on Dulles, who acted over Joint Chiefs orders

stops.name: Berlin, six months in the ruins
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the posting is attested to 1945, the months are not fixed
stops.campa: He takes the Berlin station for about six months in the flattened city, ten years after he last stood in it arguing that his firm should get out of Germany. The work is no longer intelligence against a regime. It is the sorting of the regime's survivors into those who are useful and those who are not. In October Washington dissolves the Office of Strategic Services and divides its functions between the State and War Departments. Dulles goes back to Bern, and then home to the law.
suggested_refs: The OSS Berlin station, 1945, and the dissolution order of October 1945
sources: Note: sources calling him Hitler's guest in 1933 and dating his previous Berlin visit twelve years earlier are wrong on both counts; the 1935 trip makes the interval ten years

stops.name: Capitol Hill, the Herter Committee
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: Back in civilian life he works as senior staff on the House select committee under Christian Herter reviewing the aid programme that becomes the Marshall Plan, and he settles into the Georgetown dinner circuit where a good deal of postwar American foreign policy is worked out between courses. The following year he advises Thomas Dewey's presidential campaign alongside Foster, on the general assumption that Dewey will win and both brothers will be in the government by January. Dewey loses.
suggested_refs: The Herter Committee's 1947 European survey
The Georgetown Set of postwar Washington

stops.name: Washington, the report on the agency
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: With William Jackson and Mathias Correa he writes a study of the two-year-old Central Intelligence Agency for the National Security Council, and the study is an indictment: the organization is wrong, the direction is wrong, the performance is poor, and the covert side is neither properly run nor properly staffed. He is fifty-six, in private practice, writing about an institution he does not work for. The report is classified. In January 1951 the man who wrote it takes over the agency's covert side.
suggested_refs: The Dulles-Jackson-Correa Report to the National Security Council, 1949

stops.name: 2430 E Street, Deputy Director for Plans
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Walter Bedell Smith brings him in on the fourth of January 1951 to run Plans, which is the agency's word for covert action, and by the twenty-third of August he is Deputy Director of Central Intelligence. The headquarters is a scatter of wartime sheds and offices in Foggy Bottom, at 2430 E Street, temporary structures that have outlived the war that put them up. In these years Plans grows faster than the whole of the rest of the agency. Dulles is fifty-seven.
suggested_refs: The original CIA headquarters at 2430 E Street NW, Foggy Bottom

stops.name: The White House, the two brothers sworn in
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Foster takes the oath as Secretary of State on the twenty-sixth of January. Allen takes his as the first civilian Director of Central Intelligence a month later, on the twenty-sixth of February. For six years the diplomacy of the United States and its secret operations are directed by two sons of the same manse in Watertown, who can settle a question between them by telephone with no record made of it. Their sister Eleanor Lansing Dulles is at the State Department as well, on the German desk.
suggested_refs: The simultaneous tenures of John Foster Dulles at State and Allen Dulles at the CIA, 1953-1959

stops.name: 2430 E Street, the order for Tehran
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the month of the operation
stops.campa: He approves TPAJAX, the joint American and British operation to remove Mohammad Mosaddegh, who has nationalized Iran's oil, and to restore the Shah to full power. Dulles never goes to Tehran. Kermit Roosevelt goes, with money and a network of paid crowds, and on the nineteenth of August Mosaddegh's house on Kakh Street is shelled and he surrenders to the army the following morning. In Washington the operation is judged a total success and cheap. The same men are asked to do it again in Guatemala within the year.
suggested_refs: The 2013 American acknowledgment of the CIA's role in the 1953 coup
sources: Stephen Kinzer, All the Shah's Men (2003)
Atlas corpus, mohammad_mosaddegh.journey.json, stops 'Kakh Street, the house shelled' and 'Tehran, the surrender the next morning'

stops.name: The White House, the plan for Guatemala
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the month of authorization
stops.campa: Eisenhower authorizes PBSUCCESS, the operation against Jacobo Arbenz, whose land reform has expropriated uncultivated holdings of the United Fruit Company. Both Dulles brothers had done work for United Fruit as partners at Sullivan and Cromwell. Nobody in this room has to say that the company's interest and the national interest are the same thing, because the men who would have to distinguish between them are the same men. The base for the operation is built at Opa-locka in Florida and answers back to this building.
suggested_refs: The 'Lincoln' base at Opa-locka, Florida, operational centre of PBSUCCESS; Dulles's own presence there is not attested

stops.name: 2430 E Street, three more airplanes
stops.date_confidence: attested to 22 or 23 June
stops.campa: The invasion column under Carlos Castillo Armas is stalling and the air support has been shot down or grounded. Dulles arranges an emergency purchase and delivery of three more P-47 fighters. Historians of the coup treat those three aircraft as the point on which it turned. On the twenty-seventh Arbenz leaves the presidential palace at eight in the evening and power passes not to Castillo Armas but to a military junta under Colonel Carlos Enrique Diaz; Castillo Armas is not elected president of the junta until the seventh of July.
stops.quote: United Fruit's attorney was US Secretary of State John Foster Dulles, and his brother Allen Dulles was the head of the CIA. On behalf of United Fruit Company, the two Dulles Brothers conspired to overthrow President Jacobo Arbenz of Guatemala.
stops.quote_source: Jeffrey Sachs, remarks at the United Nations Food Systems Pre-Summit, October 2021
suggested_refs: The bombing of the Matamoros Fortress, Guatemala City, ordered 18 June 1954; Dulles was not present

stops.name: The Senate Office Building, the break-in
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date: the episode spans 1953 and 1954 and was declassified only in 2004
stops.campa: Joseph McCarthy begins subpoenaing CIA personnel and Dulles goes to Eisenhower to have it stopped, which Eisenhower does. What is not known for another fifty years, until the documents are declassified in 2004, is the rest of it: that on Dulles's orders the agency burgled McCarthy's Senate office and fed him false information, so that he would repeat it in public and be discredited by it. He repeats it. The agency's charter gives it no domestic operational authority of any kind.
suggested_refs: The 2004 declassification of CIA operations against Senator Joseph McCarthy

stops.name: Arlington, his brother's grave
stops.date_confidence: inferred: Foster died 24 May 1959 and the burial followed within days
stops.campa: Foster dies of cancer at Walter Reed on the twenty-fourth of May, having given up the State Department a month before, and is buried at Arlington among the graves of an older Washington. The six years in which two brothers held the open and the secret halves of American power between them end there. Eisenhower, who had leaned on Foster more than on any other man in his cabinet, attends the burial. Their grandfather John Watson Foster lies in the same cemetery.
suggested_refs: The grave of John Foster Dulles, Arlington National Cemetery; their grandfather John Watson Foster lies there also

stops.name: Langley, the cornerstone
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Ground is broken in the Virginia woods above the Potomac for a headquarters purpose-built for the agency, and Eisenhower lays the cornerstone. Dulles, who has pushed for the building for years and is often credited with the act itself, stands beside him. The campus is designed so that the people who work in it need never leave it during the day, and its address will become the ordinary English word for the thing that happens inside. The Foggy Bottom sheds, put up as temporary structures for a war fourteen years over, will come down.
suggested_refs: The cornerstone of the CIA headquarters at Langley, laid 3 November 1959
sources: Wikipedia, 'George Bush Center for Intelligence' (Eisenhower laid the cornerstone)

stops.name: 2430 E Street, the plane that did not come back
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The agency has been overflying the Soviet Union since 1956 with an aircraft it commissioned and built itself, the U-2, on the assumption that nothing the Soviets have can reach that altitude. On the first of May a surface-to-air missile brings one down over Sverdlovsk and the pilot, Francis Gary Powers, comes down alive. Eisenhower has already put out a cover story about a lost weather flight. Khrushchev lets him finish telling it before producing the pilot. The Paris summit collapses two weeks later.
suggested_refs: The U-2 programme, developed under CIA direction from 1954 and operational from 1957

stops.name: Washington, the State Department: Lumumba comes asking
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Patrice Lumumba, prime minister of a Congo seven weeks independent, is in Washington asking the State Department for support against the secession of Katanga, and the reception is cool. Dulles has already told his own officers that Lumumba's removal is an urgent and prime objective. Within weeks the agency allocates something on the order of a hundred thousand dollars toward killing him. It never does the thing itself. In January Lumumba is flown to Katanga, handed to his enemies, and shot.
suggested_refs: The 1975 Church Committee findings on CIA assassination planning against Lumumba
sources: Atlas corpus, patrice_lumumba.journey.json, stop 'Washington, the State Department' (canonical pin 38.8951, -77.0479)

stops.name: 2430 E Street, the Cuban brigade
stops.date_confidence: inferred: planning runs from 1960 into 1961; no single date marks the plan's completion
stops.campa: The plan for Cuba is built in this building through 1960 under Eisenhower and handed to a new president who has been in office ten weeks. Fourteen hundred Cuban exiles are trained in Guatemala. The assumption written into the plan is that the landing will touch off a rising, and that if it does not, a president will not stand and watch the men on the beach be killed, and will send in whatever is needed. John F. Kennedy has said in writing that no American forces will be used.
suggested_refs: The CIA in-house Official History of the Bay of Pigs, partially declassified; authorship and release date unconfirmed
sources: Atlas corpus, john_f_kennedy.journey.json, stop 'The White House, the Bay of Pigs'

stops.name: San Juan, the speech while the brigade lands
stops.date_confidence: attested as to his absence from Washington; the Puerto Rico engagement is reported rather than documented here
stops.campa: On the day the brigade goes ashore at the Bay of Pigs, the Director of Central Intelligence is in Puerto Rico giving a speech, a long-standing engagement he does not cancel, on the reasoning that cancelling it would itself signal something. Fourteen hundred men are on the beach and the air cover does not come. The landing fails over four days and the survivors surrender on the twentieth. He is sixty-eight and has been Director for eight years. He calls it afterward the worst day of his life.
stops.quote: the worst day of my life
stops.quote_source: Allen Dulles on the Bay of Pigs, cited in W. J. Rorabaugh, Kennedy and the Promise of the Sixties (Cambridge University Press, 2002), p. 29
suggested_refs: Playa Giron and the Bay of Pigs beachhead, 17-20 April 1961; Dulles was not present at any point

stops.name: Langley, the medal and the letter
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Kennedy drives out to Langley on the twenty-eighth of November and presents Dulles with the National Security Medal in front of the assembled agency. The next day the White House releases the resignation letter. Richard Bissell and Charles Cabell go with him; John McCone gets the office. Five years later a newspaper will report that the president had wanted to splinter the agency into a thousand pieces and scatter it into the winds, sourced to an unnamed senior official and printed three years after the president was dead. No Kennedy document says it.
suggested_refs: The plaque to Allen Dulles installed at CIA headquarters under Richard Helms
New York Times, 25 April 1966, 'C.I.A.: Maker of Policy, or Tool?', p. 1, the traced source of the 'thousand pieces' line, which no primary Kennedy document supports
sources: Note: sources placing this ceremony at the White House are in error; it took place at Langley

segments.name: The Commission and the Long Retirement

stops.name: Georgetown, the house and the book
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the residence is attested to Georgetown, the street address is not consistently given in the sources
stops.campa: He lives in Georgetown, a few streets from most of the men he has spent his career talking to, and in the second year after his removal he publishes The Craft of Intelligence, an argument for the necessity of a secret service, written largely by other hands and signed with his name. It is a defence of the profession by a man who has just been removed from it, and it stays in print. In the photographs from these years he is always the same: the pipe, the tweed, the moustache, the rimless glasses.
suggested_refs: The Craft of Intelligence (1963), continuously in print

stops.name: 200 Maryland Avenue, the Warren Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Six days after Kennedy is shot in Dallas, Lyndon Johnson names a commission under Executive Order 11130 and puts Allen Dulles on it: the only member with intelligence experience, and a man the murdered president had dismissed two years before. He attends more sessions than nearly any other commissioner. The agency, now under McCone, does not tell the commission that it had been trying to kill Fidel Castro. The report runs to eight hundred and eighty-eight pages and is delivered on the twenty-fourth of September 1964.
suggested_refs: David Talbot, The Devil's Chessboard (2015), which argues Dulles steered the commission to protect himself, a case reviewers called far ahead of the evidence
Oliver Stone's JFK (1991), which places him among the conspirators
sources: Atlas corpus, john_f_kennedy.journey.json, Dallas and Bethesda stops of 22 November 1963

stops.name: Princeton, the Madison Award
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the year is attested, the month is not
stops.campa: The American Whig-Cliosophic Society, the society he debated in as an undergraduate, gives him the James Madison Award for Distinguished Public Service, and he comes back to campus to accept it. He is seventy-three and five years out of office. Two years later he edits an anthology called Great True Spy Stories. His sister Eleanor will say, after his death, that he had at least a hundred affairs, which is a family's recollection and not a number anyone can check.
suggested_refs: The James Madison Award for Distinguished Public Service, American Whig-Cliosophic Society

stops.name: Georgetown, the last illness
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Influenza turns to pneumonia and he dies at home in Georgetown at seventy-five, the family reporting that his last years had been shadowed by Alzheimer's disease. He has been out of office for eight years and has spent them writing, editing, and answering questions about Dallas. Nixon is nine days into his presidency. The obituaries call him the architect of American intelligence and are careful around Iran, Guatemala, the Congo, and Cuba. Most of that record is still classified on the day he is buried.
suggested_refs: Stephen Kinzer, The Brothers (2013), the dual reassessment of Allen and John Foster Dulles

stops.name: Green Mount Cemetery, the grave in Baltimore
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the burial follows the death of 29 January 1969; the exact date is not given in the sources
stops.campa: He is buried not at Arlington, where Foster lies and where their grandfather John Watson Foster lies, but at Green Mount in Baltimore, a nineteenth-century garden cemetery on a hill above the city, among his wife Clover's people. There is no Dulles family plot there and no explanation on the stone. The marker gives a name and two dates. For a man who spent forty years arranging that certain things not be written down, that is either an accident or the last decision he made.
suggested_refs: Green Mount Cemetery, 1501 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore, 39.3075 -76.6072, correcting three mutually inconsistent coordinate variants in circulation
sources: Note: the description of Green Mount as a historic Dulles-Foster family burial ground is unsupported; Foster and John Watson Foster are both at Arlington
